groups.title: Tablet (162601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of folic acid deficiency, for wasting disease, for supply when the need for folic acid is increased in pregnancy and breast-feeding and intake from food is insufficient, as an aid in the treatment of pernicious anaemia (excluding anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency), for nutritional deficiency anaemia, anaemia of pregnancy, anaemia in children and anaemia caused by antiepileptic treatment in which folic acid deficiency or a metabolic disturbance is thought to be involved, and for megaloblastic anaemia related to alcoholism and liver disease.
groups.usage: For the treatment of folic acid deficiency and of deficiency caused by other medicines, adults and children aged 24 months and older: take 0.25 to 1 mg in 1 day. For the prevention of folic acid deficiency and for conditions in which the requirement for folic acid is increased, adults and children aged 24 months and older: take 0.1 to 0.25 mg in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have pernicious anaemia or megaloblastic anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have pernicious anaemia, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking aminosalicylic acid, an oral contraceptive, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (methotrexate, trimethoprim and the like), a hydantoin antiepileptic such as phenytoin, sulfasalazine or cholestyramine.

If allergic symptoms such as erythema, skin rash, itching, general lassitude or difficulty breathing, an anaphylactic reaction, loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting, oedema, weight loss, gastrointestinal disturbance, or central nervous system disturbance such as changes in sleep, poor concentration, hyperactivity, irritability, excitement, depression, confusion or impaired judgement occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Prevention and treatment of folic acid deficiency and folate-related anaemias, and supply when the need for folic acid is increased
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (162601ATB) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Tablet (347904ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of runny nose, sneezing, itching and watering of the eyes, and itching of the nose or throat caused by pollen allergy or other upper respiratory tract allergy.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose with water, at intervals of 12 hours. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age; if you have kidney impairment; if you are an older person; if you do not know whether the symptoms are caused by allergic rhinitis, a cold or another cause; if you have been diagnosed with another allergic disease such as bronchial asthma or atopic dermatitis; if nasal congestion is severe; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had an allergy caused by a medicine; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have cardiovascular disease.

If you are breast-feeding and take this medicine, do not breast-feed.

Do not take it together with another anti-allergy medicine (medicine for skin disease, oral medicine for rhinitis and the like), an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant, motion-sickness medicine, hypnotic sedative and the like), an antacid (preparations containing aluminium or magnesium), ketoconazole or erythromycin. Do not take it with fruit juices (grapefruit juice, orange juice, apple juice) or with food. Do not drink alcohol before or after taking it.

If dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, drowsiness, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, rash, itching, urticaria, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, numbness, headache, fatigue, lassitude, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, nightmares, sleep disturbance, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, palpitations, taste disturbance, oedema, chest pain, difficulty breathing, raised blood pressure or menstrual disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If agranulocytosis, reduced white blood cells or neutropenia occurs with sudden high fever, chills or sore throat, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If signs of shock (hypersensitivity symptoms such as difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, angioedema, chest pain or flushing), liver function disturbance (raised AST, ALT, gamma-GTP, ALP or LDH, jaundice and the like), dizziness or nausea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Temporary relief of runny nose, sneezing, itchy and watering eyes, and itching of the nose or throat from pollen or other upper respiratory allergy
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (347904ATB) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 203 or Quinoline Yellow WS; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking a cough medicine.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Loosening mucus and helping to bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease

groups.title: Tablet (A04700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of heartburn associated with excess stomach acid and a burning sensation in the stomach.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have difficulty taking it; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you have unexplained weight loss or persistent abdominal pain; if you have kidney disease; or if you are on haemodialysis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another stomach medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol, chloroquine, a tetracycline antibiotic, diflunisal, digoxin, a diphosphonate, fexofenadine, iron (salts), a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, sodium fluoride, a glucocorticoid, indometacin, ketoconazole, lansoprazole, a phenothiazine antiepileptic, penicillamine, a phosphate, thyroxine, a salicylate or an antacid.

Occasionally nausea, diarrhoea or headache, and rarely anaphylaxis, enzyme abnormalities, constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, flatulence (abdominal distension), vomiting, thirst, rash, itching, urticaria, peeling of the skin, fatigue, jaundice, hepatitis, angioneurotic oedema, joint pain or muscle cramps may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of heartburn associated with excess stomach acid and a burning sensation in the stomach

groups.title: Tablet (D33500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for neuralgia, back pain and stiff shoulders.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 2 times in 1 day, when pain or an attack occurs.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if the user is a baby, a young child or a child (aged 14 years or younger) with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have liver, kidney or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure and the like; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after several doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite or vertigo occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Neuralgia, back pain and stiff shoulders

groups.title: Tablet (257100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and for functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary system, the urinary system and the female reproductive system, including dysmenorrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it (rash, red spots, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if you have had asthma caused by another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you have severe kidney impairment or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; if you have glaucoma; if you have difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia; if you have functional narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract such as pyloric stenosis; if you have paralytic or obstructive intestinal obstruction; if you have severe muscle weakness or megacolon; if you have rapid heartbeat or tachyarrhythmia; if you have severe liver impairment, severe heart disease, haemorrhagic colitis, peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have bacterial diarrhoea; if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have Gilbert's syndrome (Meulengracht's disease); if you have impaired heart function (coronary insufficiency, heart failure, arrhythmia and the like); if you have or have had kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have bronchial asthma, ulcerative colitis, an overactive thyroid or fever; if you have prostatic hyperplasia; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are at risk of narrow-angle glaucoma; if you are prone to obstruction of the bowel or of the outlet of the ureter; or if you are prone to tachyarrhythmia.

Disturbance of eye accommodation may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

People who have taken other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol must not take this medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic, a tetracyclic antidepressant, an antihistamine, an antipsychotic, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide or another anticholinergic medicine (tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds), an antidopaminergic medicine such as metoclopramide, a beta agonist, propantheline, chloramphenicol, probenecid, zidovudine, flucloxacillin or cholestyramine.

If thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, cyanosis, leukopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), flushing, skin reactions, abnormal sweating, itching, dry skin, urticaria, red spots, a fall in blood pressure including shock, anaphylactic shock, drug eruption, difficulty breathing, hypersensitivity, angioedema, rash, swelling (of the throat, eyelids, lips and the like), chest tightness, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, breathlessness, burn-like blisters, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), palpitations, rapid heartbeat, vertigo, fatigue, bronchospasm, thirst, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, abdominal distension, raised transaminases, difficulty passing urine, urinary retention, dilated pupils, ciliary muscle paralysis, disturbance of accommodation (in people with severe long-sightedness), anxiety, excitement, hallucination, headache, a heavy head or abnormally high body temperature occurs, or if unexpected abdominal pain continues or worsens, or occurs with fever, nausea, vomiting, a change in bowel movement, abdominal tenderness, a fall in blood pressure, fainting or bloody stools, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary, urinary and female reproductive systems, including period pain
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (257100ATB) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day. This medicine may be taken with or without food.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea; uncommonly vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation or loss of appetite; urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills; purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count; abnormal sensation of the tongue, a change in taste, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm.

summaryTable.What it is for: Acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbed mucus secretion
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (106301ATB) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (people with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation, an analgesic, an anti-inflammatory medicine or an antirheumatic medicine; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy. In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; if you have impaired cardiovascular circulation (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); if you have liver impairment or impaired heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; if you have Reye's syndrome; if the user is aged 14 years or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are to have surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or salicylate preparation, or with methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline when they are given with this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a thrombolytic, another platelet aggregation inhibitor, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), a thiazide diuretic, a lithium preparation, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemic corticosteroid (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with an alkaline preparation (for example sodium bicarbonate or magnesium carbonate) or with a preparation that easily takes up moisture. When it is taken with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa increases and bleeding time may be prolonged through the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol.

If signs of shock (for example difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria), an asthma attack, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, excitement, liver impairment, or very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inhibiting blood clot formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, after CABG or PTCA, and reducing cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (111001ATE) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Oral Solution (130502ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria (of unknown cause) and itching of the skin.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 mg, 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 2 years to under 12 years: take 10 mg in 1 day if the body weight is 30 kg or more, and 5 mg in 1 day if the body weight is less than 30 kg. For people sensitive to adverse reactions, take it in divided doses in the morning and in the evening. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. For the recommended dose in people with kidney impairment, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; or if you have the rare hereditary defect of fructose intolerance.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; if you are an older person; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia).

Do not take it together with theophylline or ritonavir. Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine. Do not take it together with alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: nervous system effects (drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation, abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, tiredness, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation, nightmares); digestive effects (occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance, increased appetite); circulatory effects (rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia, raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations); blood effects (vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes, increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased platelets, reduced platelets); immune system and skin and subcutaneous tissue effects (photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching, rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis); eye effects (rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, back-and-forth eye movement); ear and labyrinth effects (vertigo); liver effects (occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis); kidney effects (occasionally raised BUN, sugar in the urine, blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting, urinary retention); musculoskeletal and connective tissue effects (joint pain); pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

summaryTable.What it is for: Seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin

groups.title: Powder (384300APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 sachet per dose, up to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma with another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure and the like; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness or oedema occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma or liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice with yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Pain relief in headache, toothache, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back, muscle and shoulder pain, bruises, fractures, sprains, period pain and injury pain, and reducing fever

groups.title: Tablet (578100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for tinnitus (ringing in the ears).
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 15 years and older: take 2 to 3 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, with water after meals.
groups.caution:
Children under 15 years of age must not take this medicine.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to another antihistamine, a motion-sickness medicine, a cold medicine or an antitussive-expectorant; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have difficulty passing urine such as prostatic hyperplasia; if you have glaucoma or have had heart disease; or if you have had asthma caused by a medicine.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not keep taking it for a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with a motion-sickness medicine, a cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, an antitussive-expectorant or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (medicine for rhinitis or allergy).

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, raised blood pressure, dry mouth, constipation or diarrhoea occurs, or if, rarely, signs of aplastic anaemia (bruising, nosebleed, bleeding gums, fever, pale skin and mucous membranes, fatigue, palpitations, difficulty breathing, anaemia, blood in the urine) or signs of agranulocytosis (sudden high fever, chills, sore throat) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Tinnitus (ringing in the ears)

groups.title: Tablet (A06600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet per dose: adults (aged 15 years and older) 3 times in 1 day, and ages 11 to 14 years 2 times in 1 day, before meals (between meals or after meals). Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose take the largest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4; or if the user is a young child under 7 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

If severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea or vomiting occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A06600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals (between meals or after meals). Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it within 1 hour after an antacid or after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (205002APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the detoxifying treatment of severe liver disease such as liver cirrhosis.
groups.usage: Take 2 sachets (6 g) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, dissolved in a large amount of water, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have severe renal failure (a serum creatinine value of 3 mg/100 mL or more), or if you have a hereditary problem such as Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) or to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

If a hypersensitivity reaction such as asthma occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (308000ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory swelling after surgery and injury and in milk stasis (retained breast milk).
groups.usage: Adults: on the first day take 2 tablets per dose, 4 times in 1 day; after that, as a maintenance dose, take 1 tablet per dose, 4 times in 1 day. Much about how it works in the body is still not explained and the relationship between dose and effect has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood clotting disorder; if you have severe liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; or if you are being given an anticoagulant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an anticoagulant.

If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea or constipation occurs, or occasionally loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, nausea or vomiting, or rarely nosebleed or blood in the sputum occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22300ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst or dizziness occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), or cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (157301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Those aged 16 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg) per dose; up to 2 tablets (20 mg) may be taken in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergy to soybean oil; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty swallowing food or pain when swallowing, or vomiting of blood or bloody stools; if heartburn has lasted for 3 months or more; if dizziness, drowsiness or cold sweat occurs at the same time; if you have chest or shoulder pain with shortness of breath; if chest pain occurs often; if you have unexpected weight loss, nausea, vomiting or gastrointestinal pain; if you have hypersensitivity to medicines; if you have kidney impairment, heart disease or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you are on haemodialysis; or if your body functions change after taking this medicine compared with before.

Do not take this medicine for 14 days or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, a medicine for athlete's foot or an antifungal (itraconazole, posaconazole oral suspension and the like), or a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, pazopanib and the like). Consult a pharmacist if you are being given an intravenous lipid preparation. Do not take it together with drinks containing alcohol.

If symptoms persist or worsen, or if shock, anaphylaxis, difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, swelling of the face, swelling of the throat, urticaria, reduced white blood cells, reduced red blood cells, reduced platelets (the same as delayed clotting), reduced eosinophils, anaemia, delayed clotting (general lassitude, weakness, bleeding under the skin or mucous membranes, fever), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, epidermal necrolysis, rash, urticaria (erythema), abnormal liver function, raised AST (GOT) and ALT (GPT), raised total bilirubin and LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, muscle pain, rhabdomyolysis, joint pain, muscle cramps, slow heartbeat, rapid heartbeat, chest pain, raised blood pressure, facial flushing, ringing in the ears, disturbance of consciousness, convulsions, general lassitude, headache, drowsiness, insomnia, hallucination, agitation, excitement, reduced libido, abnormal sensation, a heavy head, confusion, depression, dizziness, constipation, diarrhoea, thirst, nausea and vomiting, abdominal distension, loss of appetite, stomatitis, interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure, fever, abnormal kidney function test values (raised BUN and creatinine and the like), menstrual disturbance, interstitial pneumonia with high fever, cough, difficulty breathing and abnormal chest X-ray, bronchospasm, breast enlargement in men or taste disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (166502ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for drug poisoning.
groups.usage: Adults: take 0.5 tablet to 1 tablet (50 to 100 mg) per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil, soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an intravenous lipid preparation.

If, rarely, rash, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or stomach pain occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cough medicine.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day (every 4 to 6 hours) when needed. Take it at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take more than 4 g (8 tablets) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment or reduced heart function; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); if you have taken barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; or if you have taken alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment, kidney impairment or a blood disorder; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you take it together with warfarin, lithium or a thiazide diuretic.

If shock, anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
